title.en: Language work for Bibha Chowdhuri: antonyms, suffixes -ship -ment -hood, acronyms, clipping and the passive voice
Words that honour a woman scientist

text.en: Bibha Chowdhuri was a pioneer of Indian science, and a star was renamed Bibha in her honour. The language work of her lesson teaches us opposites, exact words, suffixes, acronyms, clipping, the passive voice and report writing.

Antonyms are words with opposite meanings. The antonym of dependent is independent, of weakness is strength, of trivial is important or significant, and of neglect is care. Use the text to check the other crossword clues.
Six exact words replace long phrases. Pioneers are the first people to start something, a physicist studies matter, energy and light, peers are people of your own age or group, luminaries are famous and important people, persistence is continuous effort and determination, and barriers are things that block your way.
The suffix -ship forms words such as membership, partnership, citizenship, professorship and leadership. It shows a state, position or relationship.
The suffix -ment forms government, entertainment, agreement and achievement from the verbs govern, entertain, agree and achieve. It makes a noun from a verb.
The suffix -hood forms childhood and brotherhood. It shows a stage of life or a bond.
An acronym is an abbreviation read as a word. In the grid, NASA stands for National Aeronautics and Space Administration, AIIMS for All India Institute of Medical Sciences, AYUSH for Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy, NIPER for National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research, and WHO for World Health Organization. ISRO and STEM are acronyms too.
Clipping makes a shorter word from a longer one. Back clipping keeps the front: exam from examination, ad from advertisement, memo from memorandum, gym from gymnasium, photo from photograph and lab from laboratory.
Front clipping keeps the end: phone from telephone, net from internet and bike from motorbike. Middle clipping keeps the middle: flu from influenza and fridge from refrigerator.
In the active voice the subject performs the action, as in 'Scientists discovered a cure'. In the passive voice the subject receives the action, as in 'A cure was discovered'. The passive is made with a form of be plus the past participle.
Use the passive when the action matters more than the doer, as in 'A cure for the disease was discovered', when the doer is obvious, as in 'The national anthem is sung at the start of the event', or when the doer is unknown, as in 'The car was stolen last night'.
In the news report on the malaria vaccine, the verbs become were recorded, was discovered, was tested, were published, were taken and was measured, because the verb must agree with its subject.
To rewrite the plant experiment, begin 'An experiment was conducted to investigate the effects of light on plant growth', and carry on with 'Various plants were placed...', 'Their growth was measured...' and 'Data was recorded daily'.
The Chandrayaan landing steps are a process, so use the present passive: the spacecraft is launched, it is positioned, its path is adjusted, it is slowed down and the rover is released.
For the report on the Zonal Science Exhibition, use the past tense, the passive voice and the third person, with a headline, the reporter's name and three paragraphs covering who, when, where, why, the competitions and the winners.
In the listening task you hear a podcast on Artificial Intelligence and choose answers on healthcare, the pandemic, renewable energy, education and accessibility. For speaking, hold a panel discussion on mobile phones with a moderator, principal, teacher, parent and student.

problem.en: Add a suffix to 'citizen' and rewrite 'Scientists measured the plants' in the passive voice.

text.en: The plants were measured by scientists.

why.en: Use were plus the past participle, and keep the doer with by if needed.

prompt.en: Explain when we use the passive voice, with an example.

requiredIdeas.en: the passive is used when the action matters more than the doer
also when the doer is obvious or unknown
a correct passive example such as The car was stolen last night

commonMisconceptions.en: Using the passive for every sentence
Forgetting the past participle after was or were

points.en: Acronyms are read as words: NASA, AIIMS, AYUSH, NIPER, WHO.
Passive voice: be plus past participle, used when the action matters more than the doer.
